topics.title: Channel 4 tries bite-size phone drama
topics.summary: Channel 4 has launched a five-part vertical drama for social media, with episodes around 90 seconds long. The experiment joins the growing market for short, phone-first storytelling.
topics.discussionPrompt: Could you make a whole episode of your life fit into 90 seconds? What would be the opening shot, the cliffhanger, and the one tiny detail everyone would talk about afterward?

topics.title: Blue Planet leans into real-world footage
topics.summary: Blue Planet III producers say they included cloudier, less polished shots to show viewers the wildlife footage is real, amid growing public concern about AI-generated images.
topics.discussionPrompt: Do you prefer nature shows that look perfectly polished, or ones that leave in the murky water and camera bumps? What makes something feel more trustworthy to you?

topics.title: Historian rechecks England's oldest pub
topics.summary: Tree-ring dating and historical research point to the George Inn in Somerset, serving customers continuously since the early 1430s, as England's oldest purpose-built pub.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you could visit a 600-year-old pub for one evening, what modern comfort would you miss first: music, menus, indoor plumbing, Wi-Fi, or being allowed to order dessert?

topics.title: Four places vie for City of Culture
topics.summary: Blackpool, Sheffield, Milton Keynes and Wrexham are shortlisted for UK City of Culture 2029. Each receives bid-development funding before a winner is selected next year.
topics.discussionPrompt: If your town got a giant culture budget, what would you make its signature event: a midnight market, local film festival, public art trail, free concerts, or something stranger?

topics.title: Water bills face a value-for-money push
topics.summary: UK ministers plan an unusual intervention in the next water-bill review, asking companies and regulators to prioritize affordability, leak reduction, and local investment.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a public service needs upgrades, what feels fairest: paying a little more now, fixing waste first, changing who runs it, or letting neighbourhoods set priorities?

topics.title: Banana breeding offers new hope
topics.summary: Researchers say a newly fertile Cavendish banana line could help develop disease-resistant varieties, addressing crop threats while raising questions about taste, farming, and biodiversity.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the familiar banana disappeared from stores, would you try a new variety immediately, demand the closest possible replacement, or turn it into an excuse to explore totally different fruit?

topics.title: Bogong moths make a remarkable return
topics.summary: Citizen-science observations suggest endangered bogong moths are rebounding across eastern Australia this spring, a hopeful sign for ecosystems that depend on the insects.
topics.discussionPrompt: What creature would you be delighted to see suddenly everywhere again: butterflies, fireflies, frogs, songbirds, ladybugs, or a surprisingly charismatic moth?

topics.title: Data-centre project sparks local debate
topics.summary: Finnish authorities halted work at planned data-centre sites after environmental concerns linked to extensive tree felling, highlighting tensions around AI infrastructure and local impacts.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a giant data centre came to your area, what would you ask about first: jobs, electricity, water, trees, taxes, or whether the waste heat could warm homes?

topics.title: Pubs consider more low-alcohol choices
topics.summary: Heineken has encouraged British pubs to consider smaller serves and alcohol-free options as changing health habits may affect demand for beer and cider.
topics.discussionPrompt: What makes a pub or café feel welcoming when you are not drinking alcohol: snacks, games, good music, comfy seats, great mocktails, or somewhere to stay late?

topics.title: AI and cancer prediction prompt questions
topics.summary: A new discussion about AI tools for predicting cancer outcomes has renewed attention on how clinicians can test new systems, explain their limits, and use them alongside human judgment.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would you rather a doctor use a very good prediction tool and explain it plainly, or keep the technology out of the room? What would build your trust?
